I am a 47-year-old woman farming in the South South. This plot is only 0.20 hectares and it is rented, so I do not want to waste money buying fertilizer or expensive seed for land that is not mine. The rains here are reliable for root crops, and I have kept my own cassava cuttings and yam setts from last season's harvest. My children and I will do all the work ourselves—clearing, making mounds, planting, weeding, and harvesting—because the plot is small and hiring labor would eat up whatever little profit I might make.
